# Issue #505: Measure version declarations in the single pinned WM1 original

## Goal
Report, do not fix. Execute only the ready one-original measurement specified by docs/research/0099-writing-version-effort.json /next_measurement. Expected gain: docs/research/0100-wm1-version-evidence.md and .json replace an unmeasured WM1 input-version question with reproducible raw declarations, their interpretation and remaining authority limits. This does not resolve semantic writing feasibility or support a 2024 fallback. No session can run LabVIEW.
## Acceptance
- [ ] Record starting commit/tree, original/parser/method input hashes and prepared-source readiness. Recheck method.json SHA256 8c3b165c33c8fb4944f10a0eaa3c384fcc90d62c3278c0c910a5f2ae8b9d4da1, original SHA256 19b5dcd98b3b2e83e2b533d9227bd07d16837f350243377292b7c0b8a935338c, and pinned pylavi revision 35d2a0318f71dcb87bb9c431dc00700ee6b9fb75 plus file.py/resource_types.py hashes from study S22/S23. On missing input or mismatch, save the exact blocker and stop; never substitute a fixture.
- [ ] Parse only @environment/actor-framework/Core/ActorFramework/Message Dequeuer/Equals Not A Refnum.vi with the pinned Resources loader. Enumerate every vers and LVSR entry, including duplicate IDs, recording resource ID, length, raw payload/hash, version-field byte offset and raw bytes, matching pinned-class decoding and decoded tuple/value. Preserve absent, malformed or conflicting declarations explicitly. Record the exact repeatable Python invocation and parser source locators; do not infer save format from filename, project version or Header.VERSION.
- [ ] Separate observed bytes, parser interpretation and authoritative original-save-version evidence. State agreement/disagreement and whether independent save-version confirmation remains unavailable; agreeing fields alone do not establish native compatibility or preservation. Compare the result to WM1's currently unknown original-version requirement without editing it.
- [ ] Write only docs/research/0100-wm1-version-evidence.md, .json and, if useful, a small replay script under the same prefix. JSON has schema_version 1, status measured or blocked, inputs, entries (an array), conclusion and limitations; blocked outcomes include a nonempty blocker. Keep original, parser, prior studies, POC files and benchmark pins unchanged. Save evidence early. No corpus scan, semantic edit, native execution, benchmark run, source/build search, product/policy/evaluator change, new owner request or git commit. Stop after one record or immediately at pin/parse failure.
- [ ] Report which exact input uncertainty narrowed and one next action warranted by the evidence, retaining any missing authority. Do not claim a writer, method readiness, fallback decision or product improvement; do not repeat closed synthetic or completion-guard reviews.
## Verification
python3 -c "import json,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path('docs/research/0100-wm1-version-evidence'); d=json.loads(p.with_suffix('.json').read_text()); assert d['schema_version']==1; assert d['status'] in ('measured','blocked'); assert all(d[k] for k in ('inputs','conclusion','limitations')); assert isinstance(d['entries'],list); assert d['status']!='blocked' or d.get('blocker'); assert p.with_suffix('.md').stat().st_size>0"
This checks committed output structure only. Run the actual pinned-source extraction separately while LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT is available; engine verification has no prepared environment. A blocked record is preserved evidence, not a successful measurement.
## Context
- docs/research/0099-writing-version-effort.md and .json: inspected by the shaper; they distinguish decisive semantic/integrity uncertainty from this ready metadata measurement and pin the exact original/parser.
- .session/reports/501.json via exports: actual accepted report, with output hashes and the missing live-loop-state limitation.
- journal/working-memory.md: delivered unsuccessful POC, closed reviews and deferred prerequisites.
- docs/perpetua/roles.md: offline role capability and separation of measurements from implementation.
## Budget
Read the two 0099 study outputs, benchmark/writing/method.json only its WM1 original/version requirements, .session/exports/manifest.json and exported #501 report, docs/perpetua/roles.md, and @environment/readiness.json. Inspect only the pinned original and bounded relevant excerpts of @environment/pylavi/pylavi/file.py, resource_types.py and directly required pinned parser definitions. No large JSON dumps, history search, project/corpus enumeration or downloads. Keep command output short; publish the one-record finding early. No live .session/loop-state.json is required: researcher staging previously omitted it, and this measurement uses explicit immutable pins.

# 0099 — Writing changes the version-effort comparison

**A full-goal total, meaningful all-version/2024 effort ratio and fallback decision are not supported by the available evidence.** The historical [0002 study](0002-delivery.md) estimates reading only: 33–99 versus 89–264 engineer-days, assuming an unverified LabVIEW 8.0–2025 range. Those are inherited engineering estimates, not measured durations or the current scope boundary. Creation, modification, preserved-version outputs and source-based rebuilds were omitted.

Starting commit `058c3abf6be57eca65394a6c2500a95ded2b26e3`, tree `c1e21ef789a7bac6701f01437068fa97a2031237`; initial tracked worktree clean. [Evidence JSON](0099-writing-version-effort.json) records SHA256s for all 25 sources actually used, separates direct observations, inherited results and new assumptions, and details costs, dependencies and checks. `.session/loop-state.json` is absent and selected history has zero records: comparison uses the committed [goal](../../goal/goal.md), explicitly without verified live-goal parity.

The [delivered POC](poc/delivery.md) parsed eight selected originals but produced no edited VI, executable semantic recipe, save-version demonstration or native validation. Its [saved blockers](poc/edit-readiness.md) concern primitive/type semantics, BDPW and compiled-cache rules. Structural framing and equal resource names/sizes do not establish semantic or round-trip compatibility. This bounded failure neither proves editing impossible nor warrants repeating its corpus search.

[Review #493](https://github.com/Kucze3205/ConnectWithLabview/issues/493#issuecomment-6840362734) clears S1–S3 on its pinned synthetic design, not native writing or readiness. The [writing contracts](../../benchmark/writing/method.json) add real outputs, independent semantic/preservation keys, original-to-output version equality and matched source/build chains. WC1/WM1/WM2/WB1 remain incomplete development specifications; their artifact inventory does not bound the goal.

| Required family | Shared reading foundation | Incremental creation/modification/rebuild work; version difference |
|---|---|---|
| Native VI/control/type artifacts, related resources and variants | Container access plus semantic graph/type/dependency decoding | Construct valid defaults and graphs; encode changes; preserve unrelated objects and confirmed consumers; establish integrity/cache rules. All versions needs evidenced format adapters; 2024 still lacks a demonstrated semantic encoder. Templates, VIM, globals, menus, LLB, tests and custom extensions remain gaps. |
| XML projects/libraries/classes/build definitions and configuration | Read declarations and references | Preserve schema/version, membership, dispatch, target/build meaning and native-member relationships. Shared XML machinery helps both scopes; normalization alone does not budget semantic writing. |
| Packages/archives and compiled distributions | Inspect manifests, members, APIs and missing-diagram limits | Create/edit valid packages; change compiled artifacts through matching sources and frozen builders. All-version toolchain/runtime combinations may add work; 2024 supplies neither absent sources nor builders. WB1 has neither. |
| Modules/targets, RT/FPGA/hardware and future families | Explicit family/target interpretation | Additional edit/build/deploy rules and independent target checks remain in both scopes. Desktop or simulation evidence cannot certify hardware behavior. |

The JSON gives eight cost drivers with units, shared/version-dependent work, dependencies and uncertainty. Reuse reading and dependency models once; charge encoding, creation defaults, preservation, packaging/build adapters and writing-validation increments separately. Extend existing benchmark infrastructure rather than re-adding it. Historical wrapper figures concern reading interfaces; MCP changes access, not compatibility. New day ranges remain unknown: no timed semantic write/rebuild sample or count of incompatible encoding/schema/target strata supports them. Machine job-hours and unavailable inputs are separate from engineer-days.

Track **original save version, emitted editing format and validation runtime separately**. Preserve/hash originals; independently freeze semantic changes, allowed file/object differences and per-file version evidence; check every emitted/propagated source against its original, or a creation's requested target. Unknown/conflicting version fields remain unverified. A separate provisioned native job must distinguish load, build, controlled behavior and target execution on frozen disposable outputs, recording conversions. Newer-runtime loading alone cannot prove same-save-version preservation.

A strict 2024-format fallback loses older/later originals; historically, 413/415 versioned RSRC inputs were outside 2024, an illustration rather than a scope or prevalence estimate. Keeping an old original alongside a converted copy prevents destruction but does not preserve the edited output's old compatibility. Supporting old-format outputs restores the corresponding encoding work. Source versions, package/build tools, modules and runtime availability remain unresolved; the recorded 2026 headless compilation neither provisions 2024 nor supplies an authoring capability. Offline editing feasibility and native compilation/execution are distinct. **No fallback is selected or presently evidence-supported; silence grants no acceptance.**

## What next

The decisive uncertainty is semantic encoding plus integrity/cache preservation and its reuse across formats. A controlled, independently authored same-version one-change pair could expose dependent changes; an eventual edited artifact also needs original-version native load/behavior checks. Neither that pair nor native capability is staged, so no decisive experiment is currently ready.

The **one smallest ready follow-up** is a version-evidence audit of WM1's exact [pinned original](../../benchmark/writing/method.json), whose prepared-file SHA256 was checked here: `19b5dcd98b3b2e83e2b533d9227bd07d16837f350243377292b7c0b8a935338c`. Exact inputs, output and resume limits are in JSON `next_measurement`; retain saved POC evidence and closed reviews.

# Starting roles

Topic E configures the loop's starting capabilities. It creates no reader, benchmark cases,
quality thresholds or new access. The role label selects `<layer>/roles/<name>/SKILL.md`
and the matching entry in that layer's `profiles.yml` (see [managed definitions](managed-resources.md)).
The Policymaker may adapt ordinary roles within the owner's limits; the evaluator verifier's
contract remains owner-controlled. Layer assignment (M2/M3, 20 October 2026): execution roles do
not see the inside of policy, so the reviewer judges the work from pinned evidence without it.

## Responsibilities and separation

| Role | Layer | Responsibility | Repository output |
|---|---|---|---|
| orchestrator (shaper) | execution | Shape one iteration and its dependencies; preserve context | `journal/` |
| researcher | execution | Investigate prepared primary sources, LabVIEW compatibility and delivery options | `docs/research/` |
| benchmark | execution | Prepare verification protocol, development cases and reproducible readiness evidence | `benchmark/` |
| implementation | execution | Implement assigned product behavior after benchmark prerequisites | Product paths declared in its profile |
| reviewer | execution | Independently inspect a pinned product or preparation change against Standards and Spec | Session report/artifacts only |
| evaluator | policy | Implement the measurement under the Policymaker's order | `policy/evaluator/` only |
| evaluator-verifier | policy | Independently check an evaluator change, including transition to real measurement | Session report/artifacts only |
| audit | policy | Measure use of the loop's environment, not product quality | `audit/` |

The Policymaker is a separate engine-selected agent in the policy layer (its skill is `policy/roles/policymaker/SKILL.md`, its permissions come from `engine.yml`), not a task profile.
Keep its existing evaluator and audit orders. The orchestrator can order researcher,
benchmark, implementation and reviewer work, but cannot order evaluator changes.

Independent review means another session with the original evidence and pinned input
trees; different provider/model names alone do not establish independence. A reviewer
reports findings and never edits the work being reviewed. The engine starts the protected
evaluator verifier after evaluator changes and pins approval to the evaluator tree.
Ordinary reviewer recommendations do not bypass the owner change gate.

## Work sequence

1. Research concrete uncertainties using existing source material. Let agents compare
   technical delivery options, including MCP, against the goal rather than choosing a
   delivery form for the owner to organize.
2. Prepare the repeatable verification method and development evidence with the benchmark
   role, following [the evaluation contract](evaluation.md). The first examples are a
   starting corpus, not a scope reduction. Public examples cannot be claimed as private
   or unseen by a model.
3. Give the reviewer a pinned preparation tree, protocol and original-source evidence.
   If executable measurement changes are needed, suggest them to the Policymaker for an
   evaluator order; the engine then requires the separate evaluator verifier's pass.
4. Obtain owner acceptance of the independently checked method and evidence through the
   existing change gate before issuing product implementation. Put links and exact tree
   identities in the implementation task's context. Missing benchmark prerequisites stay
   explicit; role availability does not establish readiness.
5. Implement and independently review product changes against the accepted method. Keep
   evaluation changes in their own sessions. Acceptance thresholds and a goal gate still
   require the owner's separate decision.

Task dependencies sequence sessions. Authoring and reviewing may occur in later iterations
when that gives the reviewer a clearer accepted snapshot. For unmerged input, pass the
candidate branch/tree through the engine's `start_branch` and staged artifacts; list the
baseline SHA, candidate SHA and specification in the task. Report missing input as blocked.
The engine's current owner gate still decides merges; this document does not install an
automatic product-review merge gate.

## Available tools and limits

The four goal-work profiles (researcher, benchmark, implementation, reviewer) are offline. They use the broker's Read/Glob/Grep/Write/Edit tools
and allowlisted git/Python commands. The engine separately permits session reports and
artifacts, so `reviewer.write: []` allows a report while preventing repository edits.
Profiles define filesystem writes, not data confidentiality: readable repository content
is not hidden from implementation sessions.

The existing preparation step pins public pylavi and NI Actor Framework sources. In
routed sessions the broker exposes their read-only cache as `@environment/` to text tools;
commands see `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT=/resources/environment`. Begin with `readiness.json`.
Python can inspect binaries, XML and prepared parser sources without downloads. Reuse
only packages actually present; request unavailable dependencies rather than assuming them.

The established NI headless workflow proves a bounded cloud automation path, not access
from role commands. No role receives Docker, the host daemon, desktop automation, model
credentials, GitHub credentials, MCP, subagents or a paid API. A native experiment needs
staged trusted results or an approved capability/engine change with a readiness check.
Likewise, additional web material needs a prepared source or explicitly accepted access;
changing `internet` alone does not add a web tool to the routed broker.

Withheld evaluation cases and answer keys cannot be secured by a folder in this public
repository or its history. Preparation may specify their separation but must request and
verify the needed restricted storage/execution before claiming a withheld evaluation.
The evaluator-only write permission does not itself hide evaluator files from product roles.

The new profiles stay within existing `engine.yml` limits. Missing capabilities use the
engine's owner-request protocol; ordinary role/profile adjustments go to the Policymaker.
No broadening of accepted limits is made here. Topic F decides those boundaries; topic G
decides remaining operating parameters. Existing model routing classes are reused for the
new role names, preserving all three provider candidates and quota fallback.

and `~/.claude/skills`, and the installed Matt Pocock plugin 1.2.3. Personal research,
implement and code-review workflows provide suitable bases; the plugin equivalents add
no needed capability. Existing project orchestrator, audit, evaluator and evaluator-verifier

provenance, not runtime dependencies.
